scenario: A coastal engineer is measuring sediment displacement along the Washington coast following winter storm surge events. The baseline terrain is a 2018 USGS 3DEP LiDAR DTM referenced in US survey feet (mean elevation 150 ft). The delivered raster directly subtracted the feet baseline from the metre post-storm DTM without converting units, reporting severe artificial erosion across the entire beach.
oracle: Delivered difference mean is -104.5 m instead of the true mean of -0.22 m; analyst subtracted feet directly from metres without applying 0.3048 conversion.

The source elevation model was acquired by a regional county consortium with vertical units in international feet (elevations between 4,500 ft and 6,500 ft). The delivered DTM was labeled as metres, but the contractor multiplied the feet elevations by 3.28084 (the metre-to-foot factor) instead of multiplying by 0.3048, producing an impossible peak elevation exceeding 21,000 metres.

scenario: A surveyor in coastal North Carolina submitted a digital elevation model for tidal flood inundation planning. The contract required orthometric heights referenced to NAVD88. oracle: Delivered raster is missing the declared geoid undulation correction of -31.5 m; all output elevations have a constant datum bias of -31.50 m relative to NAVD88.
